title: License Plate Readers Were Already a Privacy Nightmare. Then Came SignalTrace.    - ACLU of Northern California
summary: The ACLU of Northern California warns that Leonardo's new SignalTrace product would augment ALPR cameras with sensors that capture electronic signals from personal devices (phones, wearables, Bluetooth, etc.) to build 'electronic fingerprints' linked to vehicles and license plates. The piece argues this expands existing ALPR civil-rights harms and violates constitutional privacy protections, urging communities and policymakers to push back.

key_quotes.quote: Surveillance vendor Leonardo has started pushing a product called SignalTrace, marketed specifically to police, which would add new sensors to ALPR cameras to detect, collect, and store electronic information from almost every personal device you carry with you. All without a warrant.
When multiple devices consistently move together with a vehicle, SignalTrace's algorithms link them to that vehicle's license plate and time-stamped location data.

This wealth of personal information allows Leonardo to create a unique "electronic fingerprint" for each individual, which it can then sell to law enforcement, border security, and other government agencies.
